306.t: Burying people in their favorite clothes
306.s: They discuss burying the dead in favorite suits, Masonic caps or even shoes, as in the case of a preacher.
306.q: Oh yeah, sure, sure. They're bearing with whatever they desire or like. You understand, that's what they actually, remember, I know one fellow's bearing with his shoes on, because he was a preacher, you know. They're bearing with his shoes on.

306.t: How bodies were laid out and put in the coffin in the old days
306.s: Bodies lay on a cot-like stretcher until the undertaker brought the coffin. Rene contrasts today's baskets.
306.q: At that time, it was laid out on like a stretcher like. You know, something looked like a sleeping cot like. They would have a, yeah, you see? And then that morning before the funeral, they'd come back and bring that coffin. See? They didn't have, like now, they just carry them in the coffin. But…

306.t: Laying out the body: veil, flowers and candles
306.s: Rene describes the veil, where flowers were placed and the three candles representing God, Father and Son, now replaced by electric bulbs.
306.q: Well they wouldn't have nothing more than a sort of a veil over him, you know. That's all kind of flies and things, you know. They have a veil over them and some people would have, you know, bring flowers or something. Well they would set the flowers right at the head or at the feet, you know. They…

306.t: Old body preparation, embalming and mummified bodies
306.s: Rene recalls a poor man's body laid out and discusses modern embalming and petrified bodies he saw at the cemetery.
306.q: A lot of them, they're supposed to remember everything, God, Father, Son, the Holy Spirit, that's what it's supposed to be. And they don't put them candles anymore now, you know. The lights. Oh. Electric bulbs now, you see. They used to have candles. And I tell you what happened too, in them days…

306.s: Rene describes the talks, viewing, prayers and graveside service.
306.q: What's the same as daughters? We have a, like the night of the week, we have a little short talk. This day of funeral we have such subject as why does man die? And where does man go? Will man live again? Shoulder live a true resurrection. Why man did this, this is being our first father's enemies.…

306.t: The wake: family, red beans, drink and lodge suppers
306.s: Families laid out the dead at home and fed visitors red beans and rice, beer, wine and coffee all night. Rene mentions society suppers.
306.q: The family? Well, they used to lay them out in the house. They used to lay them out in the house. See, the family would be there. And they'd have work all night. Some of them used to have spaghettas. I used to look for them kind of, quick. The last week I made it right here on, on Saratoga between…

1014.t: His premonition, wishes for his music, and prayer in the hospital
1014.s: He told her he would not come home for Christmas, spoke of grandchildren, Shirley and his music, planned his funeral music, and they prayed with his mother's rosary and crucifix.
1014.q: Well, he spoke of his past. We had in the past year, though, spoke much about his past, his life. He had mentioned... He pleaded with me not to take him to the hospital. He felt it would be his last trip in. And I told him I wouldn't never take him under his consent, other than he would be out.…

1014.t: Choosing his burial place with his wife and mother
1014.s: They visited the graves on All Saints Day; he would be buried in the same grave as his late wife Jeannette and his mother, and she visits daily.
1014.q: Yes. He had, when we went on All Saints, All Souls Day, I took him to the graveside and put flowers on Jeannette's grave, his wife's grave, late wife's grave, and on his mother's grave. They were both buried in the same place. And he said, this is where I'm going to be. Not here. He didn't say to…

1014.s: Interruption to keep the children quiet, then a detailed account of his final hours, internal bleeding, her holding him, and his serene passing, with his earlier vision of the gates.
1014.q: Keep them up for a while. Okay? Tell them to stay out. They'll make any notes for a few minutes. Shh! Just for a few minutes, okay? Just for a few minutes.

567.s: White explains the bell is rung for Sunday school and services, tolled for a death, and tolled every half hour before a funeral.

873.s: Lawrence describes how long wakes last, rooms, food and no drinking; Allen ends the interview.
